text: Thank you very much, Wolfgang, and good afternoon to all of you. The Vice President and President Nagel and I welcome you to the press conference.

text: and express our gratitude to all of them for the excellent organization of today's meeting of the Governing Council.

speaker: presidenta
text: And I hope that you have felt that hospitality and that welcoming embrace by the Bundesbank.

speaker: presidenta
text: The Governing Council today decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.

speaker: presidenta
text: The conflict in the Middle East continues to generate inflation pressures,

speaker: presidenta
text: and inflation is set to remain well above target for an extended period.

speaker: presidenta
text: Today's decision underscores our commitment to setting monetary policy to ensure that inflation stabilizes at our 2% target in the medium term.

speaker: presidenta
text: The baseline of the new ECB staff projections

speaker: presidenta
text: sees headline inflation averaging 3% in 2016,

speaker: presidenta
text: 2.5% in 27 and 2.1% in 28. For inflation, excluding energy and food, the baseline

speaker: presidenta
text: foresees 2.5% in 26, 2.6% in 27 and 2.3% in 2028. Compared with June, the baseline projection

speaker: presidenta
text: for inflation in 26 is unchanged, while it has been revised up for 27 and 28.

speaker: presidenta
text: The baseline projection for economic growth is 0.9% for 26, 1.4% for 27, and 1.5% for 28.

speaker: presidenta
text: And this is an upward revision for both 26 and 27, mainly reflecting the greater than expected resilience of the euro area economy.

speaker: presidenta
text: The outlook remains highly uncertain, with risks to the upside for inflation and to the downside for economic growth.

speaker: presidenta
text: In relation to the energy shock, the updated scenarios put together by staff illustrate the broad range of outcomes for how growth and inflation would evolve under different assumptions about its intensity and duration, as well as its indirect and second-round effects.

speaker: presidenta
text: With today's decision, we remain well positioned to navigate the uncertainty caused by the conflict.

speaker: presidenta
text: We will follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach to determining the appropriate monetary policy stance.

speaker: presidenta
text: In particular, our interest rate decisions will be based on our assessment of the inflation outlook and the risks surrounding it in light of the incoming economic and financial data,

speaker: presidenta
text: as well as the dynamics of underlying inflation

speaker: presidenta
text: and the strength of monetary policy transmission.

speaker: presidenta
text: We are not pre-committing to a particular rate path.

speaker: presidenta
text: The decisions taken today are set out in a press release available on our website.

speaker: presidenta
text: And I will now outline in more detail how we see the economy and inflation developing

speaker: presidenta
text: and will then explain our assessment of financial and monetary conditions.

speaker: presidenta
text: The economy proved resilient in the second quarter, despite headwinds from the energy shock.

speaker: presidenta
text: Growth was broad-based across countries and sectors.

speaker: presidenta
text: This pattern is likely to have continued into the third quarter.

speaker: presidenta
text: Manufacturing continues to perform solidly as governments spend more on defense and infrastructure. Consumer confidence has rebounded from low levels, helping services recover from the initial energy shock.

speaker: presidenta
text: Increased AI-related activity is visible in digital services, business investment and exports.

speaker: presidenta
text: The labour market has remained robust, with the unemployment rate unchanged in July at 6.4%.

speaker: presidenta
text: Growth in employment and the labour force continues to slow, while productivity has gradually picked up.

speaker: presidenta
text: Looking ahead, the near-term growth outlook has improved, compared with the last round of staff projections,

speaker: presidenta
text: projections, reflecting in particular the resilience of private consumption and public

speaker: presidenta
text: spending.

speaker: presidenta
text: Over the medium term, consumption should be supported by gradually falling energy prices

speaker: presidenta
text: and a strong labour market.

speaker: presidenta
text: Growth will increasingly be bolstered by business and housing investment.

speaker: presidenta
text: growth should benefit from rising foreign demand, but is being held back by competitiveness

speaker: presidenta
text: challenges and uncertainty about global trade policies. Higher potential growth requires

speaker: presidenta
text: structural reforms and has to be underpinned by sound public finances. Simplifying and harmonizing

speaker: presidenta
text: rules across the EU's single market, accelerating the energy transition, and completing the

speaker: presidenta
text: savings and investments union are key building blocks.

speaker: presidenta
text: As the process for agreeing on the legal framework for the digital euro moves into its final

speaker: presidenta
text: stage, we reiterate the importance of reaching agreement on the single currency package as

speaker: presidenta
text: quickly as possible.

speaker: presidenta
text: Fiscal responses to the energy shock should be temporary, targeted and tailored.

speaker: presidenta
text: Looking now at inflation.

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation increased to 3.3% in August from 2.9% in July.

speaker: presidenta
text: Energy price inflation rose to 14.3% after 10.3% in July.

speaker: presidenta
text: This increase is likely to reflect, in particular, a strong contribution from refining margins

speaker: presidenta
text: on liquid fuels, as well as higher energy commodity prices.

speaker: presidenta
text: Food price inflation remained unchanged at 1.2%.

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation excluding energy and food edged down to 2.4% in July, with goods inflation

speaker: presidenta
text: increasing from 0.9% to 1.2% and services inflation falling from 3.3% to 3.0%.

speaker: presidenta
text: measures of underlying inflation were broadly stable in July. Wages do not show a material

speaker: presidenta
text: response to the energy shock at this stage. Compensation per employee grew at an annual

speaker: presidenta
text: rate of 3.3% in the second quarter, down from 3.5% in the first quarter. Rising labour productivity

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta
text: quarter. At the same time growth in unit profits rose from 0.3% to 2.2%. Looking ahead the ECB's

speaker: presidenta
text: wage tracker points to a modest uptick to 2.7% in negotiated wage growth in the first half of

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation expectations over shorter horizons remain at elevated levels, but most measures

speaker: presidenta
text: of longer-term inflation expectations stand at around 2%, supporting the stabilization

speaker: presidenta
text: of inflation around target in the medium term.

speaker: presidenta
text: The conflict in the Middle East and recent developments in Russia's unjustified war

speaker: presidenta
text: against Ukraine have pushed the path of energy prices up further.

speaker: presidenta
text: This is likely to keep headline inflation well above target

speaker: presidenta
text: into the first half of 2027.

speaker: presidenta
text: Thereafter, energy inflation should decline and turn negative

speaker: presidenta
text: up to mid-2028, bringing headline inflation down.

speaker: presidenta
text: Higher energy prices are expected to feed through gradually to core and food price inflation.

speaker: presidenta
text: The improved economic outlook should also contribute to slightly higher core inflation,

speaker: presidenta
text: which is expected to keep rising until early 2027

speaker: presidenta
text: and stay elevated for the rest of the year before moderating in 2028.

speaker: presidenta
text: overall headline inflation is expected to return to a round target towards the end of 2027 supported by the effects of higher interest rates we will continue to monitor closely the size and

speaker: presidenta
text: persistence of the energy price increase and how it feeds through to price and wage setting

speaker: presidenta
text: inflation expectations, and overall economic dynamics.

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta
text: The risks to the growth outlook are to the downside.

speaker: presidenta
text: This is due in particular to the Middle East conflict and developments in Russia's unjustified war against Ukraine.

speaker: presidenta
text: renewed disruption of energy supplies could cause energy prices to rise further and for longer than currently expected this would weigh on real

speaker: presidenta
text: incomes spending and investment a worsening of global financial market

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta
text: and thereby dampen demand.

speaker: presidenta
text: A resurgence of trade tensions between major economies

speaker: presidenta
text: could also further disrupt supply chains,

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta
text: The risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside. This is due in particular to the Middle East conflict

speaker: presidenta
text: and developments in Russia's unjustified war against Ukraine.

speaker: presidenta
text: The energy shock could intensify further,

speaker: presidenta
text: and its effects on other prices and wages

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta
text: Gas prices, in particular, could increase in the event of further supply disruptions or an unusually cold winter coinciding with low storage levels.

speaker: presidenta
text: The longer energy prices stay high, the more likely they are to drive up broader inflation

speaker: presidenta
text: through indirect and second-round effects.

speaker: presidenta
text: Renewed trade tensions could give rise to more fragmented global supply chains, curtail the supply of critical raw materials, and worsen capacity constraints in the euro-area economy. me. Extreme weather events, potentially reinforced by intensifying El Nino conditions and the

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta

speaker: presidenta
text: sustainably, or if indirect or second-round effects from the recent energy price shock

speaker: presidenta
text: proved less pronounced than anticipated.

speaker: presidenta
text: More volatile and risk-averse financial markets could weigh on demand, and thereby lower inflation as well.

speaker: presidenta
